key_insight: Rather than predicting absolute MOS scores, the paper reframes image quality assessment as a relational, directional task and trains a model to predict spatially-aware distortion maps using synthetic, self-supervised distortions—removing the need for costly human labels.
problem_solved: MOS-based IQA is expensive, subjective, and provides no localized guidance; this work provides scalable, interpretable, pixel-level distortion assessment and relative comparisons between images without manual annotation.
method: Reformulate IQA as relational/directional prediction (which image/region is more distorted) instead of absolute scoring.
Use a self-supervised synthetic distortion engine to generate diverse, localized distortions for training data, eliminating manual MOS collection.
Train a distortion prediction network to output spatially-aware distortion maps and pairwise relational labels (rankings/directions) for robust, interpretable assessment.
impact: Enables scalable, annotation-free IQA that gives pixel-level diagnostic feedback useful for image restoration, model debugging, and automated dataset curation—speeding development cycles and improving interpretability.

paper_title: Pixel Perfect: Relational Image Quality Assessment with Spatially-Aware Distortions
paper_authors: Fadeel Sher Khan, Long N. Le, Abhinau K. Venkataramanan, Seok-Jun Lee, Hamid R. Sheikh
